How to Calculate Sales Tax

Sales tax is generally calculated by applying a tax rate to the taxable purchase price. The final amount you pay is the original price plus the applicable sales tax.

Ad space (in-content)

The basic sales tax formula

To calculate sales tax, multiply the taxable purchase price by the sales tax rate expressed as a decimal.

For example, a 7% sales tax rate is written as 0.07 when used in the calculation.

Example

If a taxable purchase costs $100 and the applicable sales tax rate is 7%, the sales tax would be $7 and the total would be $107.

Actual sales tax rules can vary depending on location, product type, exemptions, and other applicable rules.

State and local sales taxes

In many locations, the applicable rate can include both state and local components. The combined rate depends on where the purchase is made and the applicable tax rules.
